data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim states that preference should go to 'the theory subjected to the most rigorous scrutiny, regardless of outcome.' Taken literally, this entails preferring a theory that was severely tested and FAILED over one that was lightly tested and survived—since the failed theory was subjected to more rigorous scrutiny and the claim explicitly disregards outcome. This is a reductio of the proposal: it dissolves the tension by destroying the distinction between corroborated and refuted theories. Compounding this, the mechanism section contradicts the claim by saying we focus on 'the theory that has survived the hardest tests'—introducing an outcome condition ('survived') that the claim explicitly set aside ('regardless of outcome'). The target is internally inconsistent and yields an absurd prescription.
